soundness_flags.label: def:exposed-order / d=0 branch
soundness_flags.one_line: d is allowed to equal zero, but k_star is defined as a maximum over the empty set and its declared space is then empty; give k_star a d=0 convention or restrict that definition to d>=1.

soundness_flags.label: Lemma 3 (lem:symmetric-reduction)
soundness_flags.one_line: It is labelled a corollary of thm:degree-frontier but drops that theorem's d|n condition, while the honest scope expressly leaves the unequal-block extension unproved.

soundness_flags.label: Open-ended Question 1 (oeq:sharp-constant-and-representers)
soundness_flags.one_line: “Every asymptotically minimax unbiased estimator arises from” a block-program minimizer has no defined estimator class, asymptotic regime, or equivalence/locality relation, so it does not yet pose a determinate question.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:degree-frontier
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The matched lower-bound theorem is currently asserted only along sequences with d>=1 and d|n.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The frontier is a conditional claim for divisible block sequences; extending it to arbitrary n is outside the present theorem.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:degree-frontier
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Constants depend on fixed beta and fixed p in (0,1), with no uniformity near contrast cancellations or the assignment-probability boundary.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The stated rate is conditional on fixed (beta,p), not a uniform triangular-array result in beta or p.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Causal Inference 11(1), 2023, official open-access article
source_verification_receipts.locator: §3.1, §3.2, Eq. (3.3), Eq. (4.4), Theorems 1–2, and discussion immediately after Theorem 2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The primary article defines maximum in/out degree and Ymax coefficient mass, gives SNIPE in Eq. (4.4), proves its coarse variance upper bound in Theorem 1, gives a degree-free Omega(1/(n p^beta)) lower bound in Theorem 2, and explicitly attributes the degree gap to weakness in the analyses.

The paper frames design-based causal estimands as linear functionals on specified function spaces and provides Riesz-based estimators with necessary and sufficient unbiasedness and consistency conditions.
The paper studies TTE under heterogeneous additive network effects when the network is unknown, using average historical baseline measurements to obtain an unbiased low-variance estimator and design.

The paper develops a low-order pseudoinverse TTE estimator for general designs, supplies bias and variance bounds, studies clustered Bernoulli and complete randomization, and uses the bounds to select candidate clusterings.
The preprint develops covariate-adjusted low-order-interference SNIPE estimators, establishes asymptotic no-harm variance, and provides an asymptotically conservative variance estimator.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define k_star=0 when d=0 (and set the empty score/energy conventions), then state the zero-degree reduction without invoking an undefined exposed order.
Keep the symmetric corollary within d|n, or prove and state the unequal-block extension before claiming the all-n p=1/2 rate.

Make the Riesz OEQ precise by fixing the block-sequence regime and an estimator class, then ask whether every asymptotically minimax unbiased estimator is equivalent in L2(P_Z) to a blockwise Riesz-program minimizer.
